subject: SIG follow-up: records shedding, prompt retention & training controls
messages:
From: Sami Rahman <sami.rahman@medicore.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-27T08:02:00-07:00
Subject: SIG follow-up: clarification on retention and training commitments

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our security team is reviewing the SIG and had a few specific follow-ups on data handling that we wanted to confirm before we complete our questionnaire: 

1) Prompt & request logs: Do you retain raw prompts or request/response logs by default for Hosted API customers? If so, what is the default retention period and what controls do customers have to shorten that?

2) Training/Model Updates: Are customer prompts, responses, or telemetry used to train or fine-tune models at Redwood Inference? If yes, how is opt-in/opt-out handled and can a customer request that their data never be used for training?

3) Ephemeral KV / caching: We use on-the-fly prefix caching in our flows. Are those contents persisted anywhere beyond in-memory KV cache? Any scenarios where cache contents would be logged or persisted for debugging?

4) Evidence: If you have a short evidence pack or single-page statement we can attach to the SIG, that would be great. A PDF or link to the retention policy is ideal.

Can you confirm preferably today — our procurement window is tight.

Thanks,
Sami
Medicore Health
security@medicore.com

--
Medicore: Compliance team

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sami Rahman <sami.rahman@medicore.com>
Cc: Medicore Security <security@medicore.com>
Date: 2026-09-27T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: clarification on retention and training commitments

Hi Sami — appreciate the clear list. High-level answers below; looping in Neha (Security) and Rishi (Product) to provide the formal SIG language and a short evidence PDF. Will deliver a single PDF you can attach. 

- Prompt & request logs: Hosted API customers have ephemeral request logs by default. We keep request/response traces for 7 days for operational troubleshooting, then they are purged from our short-term store. Customers on Dedicated or Private can configure retention via policy (including 0 days).

- Training/Model Updates: We do not use customer prompts or responses to train or fine-tune shared models by default. Training on customer data requires explicit contractual opt-in and technical opt-in. Customers can opt out at the account level; opt-out prevents their traffic from entering any training pipelines.

- KV / caching: Runtime KV cache is in-memory and does not persist beyond instance lifecycle. We only persist cache contents for explicit debug captures (rare) and only with customer approval or when enabled on Dedicated/Private deployments with configured debug windows.

I'll get you the exact SIG table answers and an evidence pack in a follow-up in the next few hours.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
E: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai | M: +1 415-555-0127

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-27T13:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: clarification on retention and training commitments

Evelyn — drafting the SIG-ready answers below; feel free to copy/paste into the SIG spreadsheet. I also attach an internal diagram that shows our KV cache flow and retention controls. Key points: 

1) Prompt & request logs (SIG ID: DATA-RET-03):
- Default (Hosted): request/response traces retained for 7 days for troubleshooting and monitoring, then automatically deleted.
- Exceptions: aggregated telemetry (non-identifiable metrics) retained longer for platform analytics.
- Controls: Customers may request reduced retention (including immediate delete) during onboarding or via support ticket for Hosted; Dedicated/Private offers configurable retention policies.

2) Use of customer data for training (SIG ID: MODEL-USE-02):
- Default stance: No. Customer prompts/responses are not used to train or improve models without explicit, documented opt-in.
- Opt-in process: contractual amendment + technical opt-in flag at account level. Opted-in data is subject to the same retention and access controls described below.

3) KV cache and ephemeral artifacts (SIG ID: CACHE-01):
- Runtime KV caches are memory-resident and not written to persistent disks under normal operation.
- Persistent captures of KV cache occur only when a customer enables a debug capture window or for Dedicated/Private with specific configuration. Any capture is time-boxed and access-controlled.

4) Audit, KMS, and deletion evidence:
- All retention/deletion actions are logged in our audit trail (immutable logs stored in our audit subsystem).
- Keys and encryption: customer data at rest is encrypted with customer-managed keys (where configured) or Redwood-managed KMS; access is role-restricted.

5) Suggested evidence pack: short PDF confirming retention windows, a one-page opt-in statement for training, and the KV cache flow diagram. I attached the diagram as "security_evidence_kv_cache_flow.pdf". I'll convert these into a single PDF for the customer.

If Rishi can confirm the product wording around Dedicated/Private configurability, we can finalize.

-Neha
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: clarification on retention and training commitments

Hi Sami / Medicore team — attaching our consolidated SIG responses and a short evidence diagram (attached as PDF). Key items from the pack below for quick reference: 

• Retention (Hosted): request/response traces retained for operational troubleshooting for 7 days, then purged. Aggregated telemetry retained separately for analytics. Customers can request shorter retention or immediate purge via support; Dedicated/Private deployments support configurable retention policies.

• Training: Redwood will not use customer prompts, responses, or telemetry to train or fine-tune Redwood-shared models unless the customer provides explicit contractual opt-in and enables a technical account-level flag. Opt-out is supported and prevents data from entering any training pipelines.

• KV / cache: runtime KV caches are in-memory and not persisted. Persistent captures occur only during a customer-enabled debug window or on Dedicated/Private with explicit configuration. All captures are time-boxed and access-controlled.

• Evidence: Attached PDF "redwood_sig_answers_v3.pdf" includes the SIG table entries you can paste into your questionnaire and the KV cache flow diagram (also attached separately for visibility).

Next steps: Please confirm if the wording covers Medicore's needs or if you prefer alternate phrasing for the SIG spreadsheet. Happy to hop on a quick 20-minute call to walk through this.
